title: Protein for muscle growth
content: Aim for roughly 1.6 to 2.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day to support muscle building. Spread it over 3 to 5 meals. Good sources: eggs, chicken, fish, lentils, chickpeas, yogurt, cottage cheese, tofu.

title: Calorie deficit for fat loss
content: Fat loss needs a moderate calorie deficit of about 300 to 500 kcal per day. Avoid crash diets. Keep protein high, eat plenty of vegetables and fiber, and keep training strength to hold on to muscle.

title: Calorie surplus for muscle gain
content: To gain muscle, eat a small surplus of about 200 to 300 kcal per day above maintenance, combine with progressive strength training and 7 to 9 hours of sleep.

title: Hydration
content: Drink water regularly through the day, around 2 to 3 liters depending on body size, climate and activity. Drink more when sweating heavily. Pale yellow urine is a simple hydration check.

title: Pre-workout meal
content: Eat a meal with carbohydrates and some protein 1 to 3 hours before training, for example oats with banana, rice with chicken, or toast with eggs. Keep fats and fiber lower right before exercise.

title: Post-workout recovery meal
content: Within a couple of hours after training, eat protein plus carbohydrates to help recovery, for example yogurt with fruit, tuna with rice, or an omelette with bread.

title: Balanced plate
content: Build meals from half vegetables, a quarter lean protein and a quarter whole-grain carbohydrates, plus a thumb of healthy fat like olive oil, nuts or avocado.

title: Healthy snacks
content: Good snack options: fruit with nuts, Greek yogurt, hummus with vegetables, boiled eggs, a handful of almonds, or dates with peanut butter. They keep energy steady between meals.

title: Vegetarian protein sources
content: Vegetarians can meet protein needs with eggs, dairy, legumes, tofu, tempeh, quinoa and nuts. Combine legumes with grains across the day for a complete amino acid profile.

title: Sleep and recovery
content: Muscles grow and repair during rest. Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep and take at least 1 to 2 rest days per week. Persistent fatigue or pain means you should back off.

title: Weekly training structure
content: Beginners do well with 3 full-body sessions per week. Intermediates can use 4 days, for example upper/lower split. Add 2 to 3 short cardio sessions and always warm up for 5 to 10 minutes.

title: Progressive overload
content: To keep improving, gradually increase weight, repetitions, sets or difficulty over time. Increase only one variable at a time and keep good form.

title: Safety and injuries
content: Stop if you feel sharp pain, dizziness or chest pain. Warm up first, keep good technique, and see a doctor before starting if you have a medical condition, are pregnant, or have been inactive for a long time.
